boundary_rationale: A setumah closes oshb:Jer.45.5 in the parashah inventory (WLC, single-witness; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own opening on the nations-rubric that stands over the whole collection, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם (oshb:Jer.46.1, byte), matching “Yahweh’s word which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.” (web:Jer.46.1) — one of only four verses in the book carrying this exact asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu shape (sweep: 4 verses), naming Jeremiah before naming any single nation. Egypt's own header follows at once with its date folded inside the same verse, לְמִצְרַ֗יִם עַל חֵ֨יל פַּרְעֹ֤ה נְכוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה עַל נְהַר פְּרָ֖ת בְּכַרְכְּמִ֑שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכָּ֗ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַת֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.2, byte), matching “Of Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah.” (web:Jer.46.2) — Pharaoh Necoh, the Euphrates, Carchemish, and Nebuchadnezzar (spelled here נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙, the resh-family form) are all named before the battle-vision itself begins, and the fourth-year date sits header-internal rather than verse-initial. The battle-summons opens directly on the next verse with no intervening narration, עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה וּגְשׁ֖וּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.3, byte), matching “Prepare the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle!” (web:Jer.46.3), continuing אִסְר֣וּ הַסּוּסִ֗ים וַֽעֲלוּ֙ הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּכ֥וֹבָעִ֑ים מִרְקוּ֙ הָֽרְמָחִ֔ים לִבְשׁ֖וּ הַסִּרְיֹנֹֽת (oshb:Jer.46.4, byte), matching “Harness the horses, and get up, you horsemen, and stand up with your helmets. Polish the spears, put on the coats of mail.” (web:Jer.46.4) — imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants, not yet a named vocative. Shock at the rout follows, מַדּ֣וּעַ רָאִ֗יתִי הֵ֣מָּה חַתִּים֮ נְסֹגִ֣ים אָחוֹר֒ וְגִבּוֹרֵיהֶ֣ם יֻכַּ֔תּוּ וּמָנ֥וֹס נָ֖סוּ וְלֹ֣א הִפְנ֑וּ מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִ֖יב נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.5, byte), matching “Why have I seen it? They are dismayed and are turned backward. Their mighty ones are beaten down, have fled in haste, and don’t look back. Terror is on every side," says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.46.5); the verse closes on neum-YHWH, but no fresh tier-1 onset follows it at the next verse, so the formula corroborates rather than closes a unit here, and the flight continues without a break, אַל יָנ֣וּס הַקַּ֔ל וְאַל יִמָּלֵ֖ט הַגִּבּ֑וֹר צָפ֨וֹנָה֙ עַל יַ֣ד נְהַר פְּרָ֔ת כָּשְׁל֖וּ וְנָפָֽלוּ (oshb:Jer.46.6, byte), matching “Don’t let the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape. In the north by the river Euphrates they have stumbled and fallen.” (web:Jer.46.6). A rhetorical question turns the description toward an extended Nile-simile, מִי זֶ֖ה כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֑ה כַּנְּהָר֕וֹת יִֽתְגָּעֲשׁ֖וּ מֵימָֽיו (oshb:Jer.46.7, byte), matching “Who is this who rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?” (web:Jer.46.7), and Egypt's own boast is quoted inside the same figure, מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֔ה וְכַנְּהָר֖וֹת יִתְגֹּ֣עֲשׁוּ מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַֽעֲלֶה֙ אֲכַסֶּה אֶ֔רֶץ אֹבִ֥ידָה עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.46.8, byte), matching “Egypt rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He says, ‘I will rise up. I will cover the earth. I will destroy cities and its inhabitants.’” (web:Jer.46.8). A summons to the allied troops follows, עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙ וְהִתְהֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב וְיֵצְא֖וּ הַגִּבּוֹרִ֑ים כּ֤וּשׁ וּפוּט֙ תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָגֵ֔ן וְלוּדִ֕ים תֹּפְשֵׂ֖י דֹּ֥רְכֵי קָֽשֶׁת (oshb:Jer.46.9, byte), matching “Go up, you horses! Rage, you chariots! Let the mighty men go out: Cush and Put, who handle the shield; and the Ludim, who handle and bend the bow.” (web:Jer.46.9), and the scene is given its theological frame, וְֽהַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת י֤וֹם נְקָמָה֙ לְהִנָּקֵ֣ם מִצָּרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֨רֶב֙ וְשָׂ֣בְעָ֔ה וְרָוְתָ֖ה מִדָּמָ֑ם כִּ֣י זֶ֠בַח לַאדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן אֶל נְהַר פְּרָֽת (oshb:Jer.46.10, byte), matching “For that day is of the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge himself of his adversaries. The sword will devour and be satiated, and will drink its fill of their blood; for the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.” (web:Jer.46.10) — the construction לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is quoted here at the byte tier without a book-wide site count, since the adonai-skeleton token's point-aware split between the divine title and the courtly adoni address is not independently re-verified in this row. The vision's first direct address falls next, עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י צֳרִ֔י בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם לַשָּׁוְא֙ הרביתי הִרְבֵּ֣ית רְפֻא֔וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.46.11, byte), matching “Go up into Gilead, and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. You use many medicines in vain. There is no healing for you.” (web:Jer.46.11) — direct address to Egypt personified as a virgin daughter, continuing the same battle-vision rather than opening a new one, and the verse itself carries a ketiv/qere pair, הרביתי written against הִרְבֵּ֣ית read (single-witness). The unit closes on a report of shared disgrace, שָׁמְע֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ קְלוֹנֵ֔ךְ וְצִוְחָתֵ֖ךְ מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי גִבּ֤וֹר בְּגִבּוֹר֙ כָּשָׁ֔לוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו נָפְל֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.46.12, byte), matching “The nations have heard of your shame, and the earth is full of your cry; for the mighty man has stumbled against the mighty, they both fall together.” (web:Jer.46.12), echoing back to verse 6's own flight-language with its own closing image of mutual collapse. oshb:Jer.46.12 itself carries a closing petuchah in the marked-verse layer (WLC-sourced, single witness only, weak in the Prophets by owner ruling). A differently-shaped header opens the next verse, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), matching “The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt:” (web:Jer.46.13), and this row stops short of that fresh onset.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting immediately after the header, on the strength of the shift from prose superscription to imperative battle-poetry, was considered and rejected: no divine-speech-frame, woe, or direct address to a named party intervenes before the address to Egypt personified as a virgin daughter, and that address continues the same Carchemish vision through its own close rather than opening an independent scene.

boundary_rationale: The parashah inventory marks oshb:Jer.46.12 with a petuchah (WLC single witness; the Prophets addendum holds this tier-3 and never a driver). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own fresh word-event heading, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), matching “The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt:” (web:Jer.46.13) — the shape here is built on the verb דִּבֶּ֣ר ("spoke") rather than the verb hayah ("came/was") that underlies all three of the book's canonical word-event shapes, so it is disclosed as its own header device rather than folded into any of them. The heading opens directly onto a fresh summons to proclaim, הַגִּ֤ידוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וְהַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ בְמִגְדּ֔וֹל וְהַשְׁמִ֥יעוּ בְנֹ֖ף וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס אִמְר֗וּ הִתְיַצֵּב֙ וְהָכֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי אָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב סְבִיבֶֽיךָ (oshb:Jer.46.14, byte), matching “Declare in Egypt, publish in Migdol, and publish in Memphis and in Tahpanhes; say, ‘Stand up, and prepare, for the sword has devoured around you.’” (web:Jer.46.14) — imperatives addressed to the frontier garrison towns rather than to Egypt as a single named addressee. A rhetorical question follows without any new frame, מַדּ֖וּעַ נִסְחַ֣ף אַבִּירֶ֑יךָ לֹ֣א עָמַ֔ד כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֲדָפֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.46.15, byte), matching “Why are your strong ones swept away? They didn’t stand, because Yahweh pushed them.” (web:Jer.46.15), and the mercenaries' own flight is reported in their own quoted words, הִרְבָּ֖ה כּוֹשֵׁ֑ל גַּם נָפַ֞ל אִ֣ישׁ אֶל רֵעֵ֗הוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ ק֣וּמָה וְנָשֻׁ֣בָה אֶל עַמֵּ֗נוּ וְאֶל אֶ֨רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַיּוֹנָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.16, byte), matching “He made many to stumble. Yes, they fell on one another. They said, ‘Arise! Let’s go again to our own people, and to the land of our birth, from the oppressing sword.’” (web:Jer.46.16) — this verse itself carries a paseq (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). The crowd's mockery of Pharaoh is quoted next, קָרְא֖וּ שָׁ֑ם פַּרְעֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ שָׁא֔וֹן הֶעֱבִ֖יר הַמּוֹעֵֽד (oshb:Jer.46.17, byte), matching “They cried there, ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.’” (web:Jer.46.17), and the unit closes on a divine oath, חַי אָ֨נִי֙ נְאֻם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ כִּ֚י כְּתָב֣וֹר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּכְכַרְמֶ֖ל בַּיָּ֥ם יָבֽוֹא (oshb:Jer.46.18, byte), matching “As I live,” says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies, "surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, so he will come. (web:Jer.46.18) — the melekh-signature נְאֻם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ, attributing the oath to the King whose name is Yahweh of Armies, names the oath's own speaker mid-verse rather than trailing it as a closing tag; it is one of only three sites of this exact construction in the book (sweep: 3 verses). The next verse opens on a fresh direct address, כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.46.19, byte), matching “You daughter who dwells in Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity; for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.” (web:Jer.46.19), and this row stops at the oath that precedes it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating verse 13 as opening its own row alone, separate from the summons it introduces, was considered and rejected: the heading carries no content of its own once split from the proclamation it frames, matching the pattern by which the book's other prose headers open directly onto their first movement rather than standing as an isolated citation.
literature_type_guess: a second word-event heading opening a fresh summons and divine oath against Egypt
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The heading's own verb is disclosed as distinct from the shapes counted elsewhere in the book's word-event census, a per-bytes deviation rather than a silent assimilation to those three shapes. The melekh-signature sits mid-oath rather than verse-final here, unlike its second occurrence later in the nations block, so no closure-corroboration claim is made for it.

boundary_rationale: A fresh direct address opens this unit, כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.46.19, byte), matching “You daughter who dwells in Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity; for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.” (web:Jer.46.19) — יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, addressed directly to Egypt personified as a dwelling daughter, distinct from the oath just closed. A setumah stands at the close of oshb:Jer.46.19 in the paragraph-mark inventory (single-witness WLC evidence, weak corroboration in the Prophets). The heifer simile follows, עֶגְלָ֥ה יְפֵֽה פִיָּ֖ה מִצְרָ֑יִם קֶ֥רֶץ מִצָּפ֖וֹן בָּ֥א בָֽא (oshb:Jer.46.20, byte), matching “Egypt is a very beautiful heifer; but destruction out of the north has come. It has come.” (web:Jer.46.20), continuing in the third person through the hired men's own flight, גַּם שְׂכִרֶ֤יהָ בְקִרְבָּהּ֙ כְּעֶגְלֵ֣י מַרְבֵּ֔ק כִּֽי גַם הֵ֧מָּה הִפְנ֛וּ נָ֥סוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו לֹ֣א עָמָ֑דוּ כִּ֣י י֥וֹם אֵידָ֛ם בָּ֥א עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם (oshb:Jer.46.21, byte), matching “Also her hired men in the middle of her are like calves of the stall, for they also are turned back. They have fled away together. They didn’t stand, for the day of their calamity has come on them, the time of their visitation.” (web:Jer.46.21), the advancing army's sound, קוֹלָ֖הּ כַּנָּחָ֣שׁ יֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי בְחַ֣יִל יֵלֵ֔כוּ וּבְקַרְדֻּמּוֹת֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔הּ כְּחֹטְבֵ֖י עֵצִֽים (oshb:Jer.46.22, byte), matching “Its sound will go like the serpent, for they will march with an army, and come against her with axes, as wood cutters.” (web:Jer.46.22), and the felling of her forest, כָּרְת֤וּ יַעְרָהּ֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֖י לֹ֣א יֵֽחָקֵ֑ר כִּ֤י רַבּוּ֙ מֵֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מִסְפָּֽר (oshb:Jer.46.23, byte), matching “They will cut down her forest," says Yahweh, "though it can’t be searched; because they are more than the locusts, and are innumerable.” (web:Jer.46.23) — the neum-YHWH here sits mid-verse, before the locust comparison that completes the sentence, not as a closing tag. The unit closes on the same figure who opened it, הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד עַם צָפֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.46.24, byte), matching “The daughter of Egypt will be disappointed; she will be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.” (web:Jer.46.24) — בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם again, bracketing the whole span. A differently-framed divine pronouncement opens the next verse, אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֤י פוֹקֵד֙ אֶל אָמ֣וֹן מִנֹּ֔א וְעַל פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל מִצְרַ֔יִם וְעַל אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ וְעַל מְלָכֶ֑יהָ וְעַ֨ל פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְעַ֥ל הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בּֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.46.25, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Behold, I will punish Amon of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with her gods and her kings, even Pharaoh, and those who trust in him.” (web:Jer.46.25), and this row does not reach it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off the opening verse alone on the strength of its own closing mark was considered and rejected: the mark is tier-3 corroboration only, and the direct address it closes governs the addressee of the whole span through the closing verse's own return to the same figure, with no fresh direct address, woe, or divine-speech-frame change intervening.
